items.title: Lillian Hardin Armstrong Interview, 1959-07-01
items.q: Her name was Miss, uh, Violet White. So she started me taking lessons.

ctx.x: What else now? I wondered about when you first took up music. Studied music? Yes. And the first music you heard, were anybody, any other members of the family musical?

Oh, they say that my father played the mandolin, but he died when I was three years old, so I don't remember him. Oh, I see. And, oh, I, we had an organ in the front room, as they called it there. The left room. We had an old organ, and, oh, ever since I was large enough to reach it, I was trying to play it, so I used to have my cousin peddle it while I'd sit up on the stool and try to play, oh, such a terrible noise. So then I would pretend the windowsill was a piano in Oregon and play that. So when I started…
What kind of pieces did you play?
